notes: Built from publicly documented FACE-Q scale names and what those scales measure. Descriptions are paraphrased constructs; no questionnaire item text is included. For satisfaction-type constructs, 'severity' expresses the degree of dissatisfaction or concern. Constructs with 'applicable_timepoints' are only active at those timepoints (extension to SPEC §6, see seed/README.md).

constructs.label: Overall satisfaction with how the face looks
constructs.description: How the person feels about their facial appearance as a whole: in the mirror, in photos and video, first thing in the morning, and whether it fits how they feel inside.

severity_signals.none: content or positive about their face as a whole
severity_signals.mild: occasional dissatisfaction or a single feature they would tweak; no avoidance
severity_signals.moderate: regular dissatisfaction; some avoidance of mirrors, photos or video calls
severity_signals.severe: persistent distress about their face; avoidance or checking that shapes daily life

drill_down: Which features bother them most
Situations where it feels worse (photos, video calls, bright light, mornings)
How long they have felt this way and whether it is changing
What they hope will be different

pediatric.description: How the child feels about their face at school, with friends, and in photos.
drill_down: Teasing or comments from others
Whether they avoid activities or photos

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the nose
constructs.description: How the person feels about the size, shape, profile, tip and nostrils of their nose, from the front and from the side, and whether it looks in proportion with the rest of the face.

severity_signals.none: happy with or neutral about their nose
severity_signals.mild: minor niggles about one aspect (bump, tip, width)
severity_signals.moderate: clearly bothered; notices it in most photos or from certain angles
severity_signals.severe: nose is a constant preoccupation; drives avoidance of photos or profile views

drill_down: Which aspect: bridge, tip, width, nostrils, profile
Angles or lighting where it bothers them most
Whether breathing is also a concern
How long it has bothered them

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the eyes and under-eye area
constructs.description: How the person feels about the look of their eyes: eyelids, symmetry, how awake or rested they look, and the under-eye area (bags, hollows, dark circles).

severity_signals.none: content with how their eyes look
severity_signals.mild: occasionally notices tiredness or puffiness
severity_signals.moderate: regularly feels the eyes look tired, uneven or older than they feel
severity_signals.severe: eyes are a persistent source of distress; uses concealment or avoids close-up views

drill_down: Upper lids, lower lids or under-eye area
Whether people comment that they look tired
Vision or eye comfort concerns
Time of day or situations where it is worse

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the lips
constructs.description: How the person feels about the shape, fullness, symmetry and definition of their lips and the lines around the mouth.

severity_signals.mild: minor wish for a change in fullness or symmetry
severity_signals.moderate: regularly bothered by lip shape, thinness or lines around the mouth
severity_signals.severe: lips are a constant preoccupation; conceals or avoids smiling in photos

drill_down: Fullness, shape, symmetry or lines around the mouth
Whether smiling or speaking makes it more noticeable
Previous treatments and how they felt about them

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the cheeks and mid-face
constructs.description: How the person feels about the fullness, contour and symmetry of their cheeks and the area between the eyes and the mouth.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally notices flatness, fullness or unevenness
severity_signals.moderate: regularly bothered by cheek volume, sagging or asymmetry
severity_signals.severe: cheek appearance dominates how they see their face; avoids certain angles

drill_down: Volume loss, heaviness or asymmetry
Whether it is worse on one side
How it changed over time

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the chin, jawline and neck
constructs.description: How the person feels about the definition of their jawline, the size and projection of their chin, and looseness or fullness under the chin and in the neck.

severity_signals.none: content with the lower face and neck
severity_signals.mild: occasional wish for a sharper jawline or a different chin
severity_signals.moderate: regularly bothered by jowls, chin shape or neck laxity; adjusts posture or clothing
severity_signals.severe: lower face and neck are a persistent distress; avoids side views or photos

drill_down: Jawline definition, chin size or neck laxity
Whether it is more noticeable from the side or in photos
How it affects clothing choices or posture

source_refs.scale: Satisfaction with Lower Face and Jawline

constructs.label: Satisfaction with facial skin
constructs.description: How the person feels about the texture, tone, evenness, pores, lines and overall quality of the skin on their face.

severity_signals.mild: occasional bother about texture, tone or lines
severity_signals.moderate: regularly bothered by skin quality; relies on makeup or filters
severity_signals.severe: skin appearance causes persistent distress; avoids being seen without concealment

drill_down: Texture, tone, pigmentation, pores or lines
Sun-related or treatment-related changes
How much effort goes into concealing it

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the smile and teeth
constructs.description: How the person feels about their smile: how it looks, how natural and symmetric it is, and how their teeth and mouth look when they smile.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally self-conscious about their smile
severity_signals.moderate: regularly holds back or covers their smile
severity_signals.severe: avoids smiling or laughing in front of others

drill_down: Symmetry, teeth, gums or lip movement
Whether they cover their mouth when laughing
Situations where it matters most (photos, meeting people)

constructs.label: Self-confidence and feeling at ease with oneself
constructs.description: How confident, attractive and at ease the person feels in themselves day to day, and how much their facial appearance or condition supports or undermines that.

severity_signals.none: feels confident and comfortable in themselves
severity_signals.mild: confidence dips occasionally, tied to specific situations
severity_signals.moderate: confidence is regularly undermined by how they feel about their face
severity_signals.severe: pervasive low confidence; feels unattractive or diminished most of the time

drill_down: Situations where confidence drops most
Whether this has changed over the past months
What helps them feel more confident
Whether it affects work or study

pediatric.description: How sure of themselves the child feels around other children and adults, and whether their face makes them feel different.
drill_down: Whether they feel 'like the other kids'
Activities they enjoy where they feel good about themselves

constructs.label: Acceptance of one's appearance
constructs.description: Whether the person accepts and feels comfortable with how they look, or feels a persistent gap between how they look and how they want to look.

severity_signals.mild: mostly accepting with occasional wishes for change
severity_signals.moderate: regularly struggles to accept how they look
severity_signals.severe: cannot accept their appearance; strong sense of being defined by it

drill_down: Whether acceptance varies by day or situation
What would need to change for them to feel at peace
Whether others' reassurance helps

constructs.label: Mood and emotional wellbeing linked to appearance
constructs.description: Feeling low, frustrated, anxious or upset because of facial appearance, the condition, or its treatment; how much of the person's emotional life this takes up.

severity_signals.none: mood is not affected by their face or condition
severity_signals.mild: occasional bad days linked to their appearance
severity_signals.moderate: regular low mood or worry tied to appearance; recovers with distraction
severity_signals.severe: persistent low mood or anxiety about appearance affecting sleep, energy or motivation

drill_down: How often it affects mood in a typical week
Whether sleep, appetite or energy are affected
Whether they have talked to anyone about it
Whether treatment has changed this

pediatric.description: Whether the child seems sad, worried or angry about their face, and how the guardian sees this affecting them at home.
drill_down: Signs the guardian notices (withdrawal, tears, anger)
Whether it is worse around school events or photos

constructs.label: Comfort in social situations
constructs.description: How at ease the person feels meeting people, being in groups, being looked at or photographed, and taking part in social life.

severity_signals.none: comfortable socially; face does not come into it
severity_signals.mild: slightly self-aware in some settings (new people, cameras)
severity_signals.moderate: regularly uncomfortable; prefers familiar company or low-visibility settings
severity_signals.severe: social situations feel threatening; strong urge to hide or leave

drill_down: Which settings are hardest (work, family, strangers, cameras)
Whether this is new or long-standing
What they do to cope in those moments

pediatric.description: How comfortable the child is with friends, in play and at parties or group activities.
drill_down: Whether they join in or hang back
Whether they have close friends they feel relaxed with

constructs.label: Avoidance of social or public situations
constructs.description: Whether the person turns down invitations, avoids going out, avoids photos or video, or withdraws from activities because of how their face looks or works.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally opts out of photos or events
severity_signals.moderate: regularly avoids some activities or people because of their face
severity_signals.severe: withdrawn from most social life; isolation because of appearance

drill_down: Specific activities or events they have skipped
How often in the last month
Whether it affects work, study or family life
Whether treatment has changed this

constructs.label: Comments, stares and teasing from others
constructs.description: Whether the person experiences stares, questions, unwanted comments, teasing or exclusion because of their facial appearance, and how they respond.

severity_signals.none: no comments or stares that bother them
severity_signals.mild: occasional questions or looks that they brush off
severity_signals.moderate: regular comments or stares that upset them or that they plan around
severity_signals.severe: frequent teasing, bullying or exclusion; significant hurt or fear

drill_down: Who it comes from (strangers, colleagues, family, online)
How they respond in the moment
Whether it has changed over time

pediatric.description: Whether the child is teased, stared at, asked questions or left out at school or in play because of their face.
drill_down: Whether teachers or the school know
Whether the child tells the guardian when it happens
Whether they have a comeback or plan

constructs.label: Close relationships and intimacy
constructs.description: How facial appearance or condition affects closeness with a partner, family or close friends, including dating and physical affection.

severity_signals.mild: occasional self-consciousness with close others
severity_signals.moderate: holds back from closeness or dating because of their face
severity_signals.severe: relationships strained or avoided; feels unlovable because of appearance

drill_down: Whether a partner or family have noticed a change
Whether they avoid dating or affection
What support they have

constructs.label: Preoccupation with appearance
constructs.description: How much mental space facial appearance takes: thinking about it, checking it, comparing to others, and feeling unable to stop.

severity_signals.mild: thinks about it now and then; can set it aside
severity_signals.moderate: thinks about it most days; some checking or comparing
severity_signals.severe: intrusive, hard-to-control preoccupation; frequent checking or reassurance seeking

drill_down: How much of the day it occupies
Checking, comparing or reassurance-seeking behaviours
When it started or intensified
Whether it affects concentration or sleep

pediatric.description: How often the child talks about, checks or worries about their face, as seen by the child or the guardian.
drill_down: Whether they ask 'why do I look different'
Mirror or photo checking

constructs.label: Hiding or camouflaging the face
constructs.description: Effort spent concealing the face or a feature: makeup, hair, glasses, hats, masks, angles in photos, filters, or avoiding being seen in certain light.

severity_signals.mild: some concealment for special occasions or photos
severity_signals.moderate: daily concealment; uncomfortable being seen without it
severity_signals.severe: cannot leave the house or be seen without concealment; strong distress if exposed

drill_down: What they use to conceal and how long it takes
Whether anyone has seen them without it
How they would feel if they could not conceal

constructs.label: Worry about cancer
constructs.description: For cancer-related conditions: worry about the cancer coming back or spreading, about further treatment, and about what changes on the face might mean.

severity_signals.none: not worried, or worry is contained
severity_signals.mild: occasional worry around check-ups
severity_signals.moderate: worries most weeks; checks the face for changes
severity_signals.severe: constant worry that interferes with sleep, plans or daily life

drill_down: What specifically they worry about
Whether check-ups or news stories trigger it
Whether they self-examine and how often
Whether they have asked their team about it

constructs.label: Breathing through the nose
constructs.description: Ease of breathing through the nose at rest, during exercise, when lying down and when sleeping; blocked or congested feeling; snoring or mouth breathing.

severity_signals.mild: occasional blockage (colds, one side, at night)
severity_signals.moderate: regular difficulty; mouth breathes or wakes at night
severity_signals.severe: constant obstruction affecting sleep, exercise or daily comfort

drill_down: One side or both; day or night
Effect on sleep or exercise
Whether it changed after injury, surgery or treatment
Sprays or aids they rely on

constructs.label: Eating and drinking
constructs.description: Ability to chew, bite, keep food and liquid in the mouth, eat a normal range of foods, and eat in front of others without difficulty.

severity_signals.mild: avoids a few foods or eats a little more slowly
severity_signals.moderate: regular difficulty chewing, leaking or spilling; avoids eating in company
severity_signals.severe: eating is a daily struggle; weight, nutrition or social eating significantly affected

drill_down: Which foods or textures are hard
Leaking, spilling or drooling
Whether they avoid eating with others
Weight change

constructs.label: Speaking and being understood
constructs.description: Clarity of speech, being understood by strangers and on the phone, effort or tiredness when talking, and reluctance to speak because of how it sounds.

severity_signals.mild: occasionally asked to repeat; some words are harder
severity_signals.moderate: regularly misunderstood; avoids the phone or speaking up
severity_signals.severe: speech severely limits communication; relies on others or writing

drill_down: Which sounds or situations are hardest
Phone calls and strangers versus family
Whether they hold back from speaking
Speech therapy or aids

constructs.label: Facial expression and movement
constructs.description: Ability to smile, frown, raise the eyebrows, close the eyes and show emotion with the face; whether expressions look symmetric and natural.

severity_signals.mild: slight asymmetry or stiffness they notice
severity_signals.moderate: expressions look uneven or limited; people misread their mood
severity_signals.severe: cannot express emotion with the face; eye closure or lip function problems

drill_down: Which movements are affected
Whether others misread their expression
Eye closure, dryness or drooling
Whether it is improving, stable or worsening

constructs.label: Swallowing and oral control
constructs.description: Swallowing safely and comfortably, controlling saliva, and keeping the mouth closed; mainly relevant after head and neck treatment.

severity_signals.mild: occasional coughing with liquids or minor drooling
severity_signals.moderate: regular difficulty swallowing or drooling that needs managing in public
severity_signals.severe: swallowing unsafe or severely restricted; constant drooling

drill_down: Liquids, solids or both
Coughing, choking or drooling episodes
Diet changes or aids
Whether it affects eating with others

constructs.label: Pain, tightness or discomfort
constructs.description: Pain, aching, tightness, pressure or tenderness in the face or treated area; how constant it is and what it stops them doing.

severity_signals.mild: occasional mild discomfort; no medication or limits
severity_signals.moderate: regular pain needing medication or limiting some activities
severity_signals.severe: constant or severe pain affecting sleep, eating or daily function

drill_down: Where and what it feels like
What makes it better or worse
Medication use
Whether it is improving over time

pediatric.description: Whether the child says it hurts or shows signs of pain (rubbing, crying, not wanting to be touched).
drill_down: How the child shows pain
Whether pain relief is being used and helps

constructs.label: Swelling, bruising and redness
constructs.description: Swelling, bruising, redness or lumpiness in the treated area; how visible it is and whether it is settling as expected.

severity_signals.mild: slight residual swelling only they notice
severity_signals.moderate: visible swelling or bruising they feel they must explain or hide
severity_signals.severe: marked swelling or bruising affecting function or keeping them at home

drill_down: Which areas and whether it is one-sided
Trend since treatment
Whether it affects vision, breathing or eating
What they were told to expect

constructs.label: Numbness or altered sensation
constructs.description: Numbness, tingling, itching, oversensitivity or strange feelings in the face or treated area, and how much it bothers them.

severity_signals.mild: small numb patch they rarely notice
severity_signals.moderate: noticeable numbness or tingling that bothers them daily
severity_signals.severe: widespread or painful altered sensation affecting eating, speaking or comfort

drill_down: Location and extent
Whether it is changing over time
Whether it affects eating, drinking or shaving/makeup

source_refs.scale: Adverse Effects: Cheeks, Lower Face and Neck

constructs.label: Scars
constructs.description: How the person feels about scars from surgery, injury or treatment: visibility, colour, texture, width, and whether they draw attention.

severity_signals.none: scars not noticeable or not a concern
severity_signals.mild: notices scars but they do not bother them much
severity_signals.moderate: scars are visible and bother them; some concealment
severity_signals.severe: scars dominate how they see their face; significant distress or avoidance

drill_down: Which scars and where
Colour, texture or raised areas
Whether they are still maturing
Whether they use scar treatments or concealment

pediatric.description: How the child (and guardian) feel about the child's scars, including whether other children notice or ask.
drill_down: Whether other children ask about the scar
Whether the child wants to hide it

constructs.label: Unevenness or asymmetry
constructs.description: Whether the person perceives one side of the face or a feature as different from the other, and how much it bothers them.

severity_signals.mild: slight unevenness only they notice
severity_signals.moderate: asymmetry they see in most photos and that others may notice
severity_signals.severe: asymmetry is highly visible to them; strong distress or avoidance

drill_down: Which feature or side
Whether it is worse with movement or expression
Whether it has changed since treatment

constructs.label: Impact of recovery on daily life
constructs.description: In the weeks after treatment: ability to work, drive, exercise, sleep, care for others and go out; tiredness; and whether recovery is going as expected.

severity_signals.mild: minor limits (e.g., no heavy exercise yet)
severity_signals.moderate: off work or missing regular activities; needs help with some tasks
severity_signals.severe: largely housebound or dependent on others; recovery much harder than expected

drill_down: Which activities are still limited
Sleep and energy
Support at home
Whether recovery matches what they were told

pediatric.description: Whether the child is back to school, play, sport and normal sleep, and how the family is managing care.
drill_down: Days of school missed
Whether they can play as usual
How the family is coping

domains.label: Satisfaction with outcome, decision and information

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the result
constructs.description: After treatment: whether the result matches what the person hoped for, looks natural, was worth it, and whether they would choose it again.

severity_signals.none: pleased; result met or exceeded hopes
severity_signals.mild: mostly pleased with a small reservation
severity_signals.moderate: mixed; clear disappointment in one or more aspects
severity_signals.severe: regrets the treatment or feels worse than before

drill_down: What they hoped for versus what they see
Which aspect disappoints, if any
Whether they would do it again or recommend it
Whether their view has shifted as healing progresses

pediatric.description: Whether the child and guardian are pleased with the result and whether it is what they expected.
drill_down: What the child says about the change
Whether the guardian's hopes were met

constructs.label: Satisfaction with the decision to have treatment
constructs.description: Whether the person feels the decision to have treatment was right for them, made with enough time and without pressure, and whether they have any regret.

severity_signals.mild: small doubts but glad overall
severity_signals.moderate: meaningful second thoughts or felt rushed
severity_signals.severe: regrets the decision or felt pressured into it

drill_down: What influenced the decision
Whether they felt rushed or pressured
Whether they would advise someone else to do it

constructs.label: Satisfaction with information received
constructs.description: Whether the person felt well informed before and after treatment about what to expect, recovery, risks and how to care for themselves.

severity_signals.mild: a few things they wish they had been told
severity_signals.moderate: important gaps; surprised by parts of recovery or result
severity_signals.severe: felt uninformed or misled; major unexpected consequences

drill_down: What they wish they had known
Whether written or spoken information was clear
Questions they still have for the team

constructs.label: How old the face looks versus how the person feels
constructs.description: Whether the person feels their face looks older than they are or feel, which features signal age to them (lines, sagging, tiredness), and how much this bothers them.

severity_signals.none: feels they look their age or younger; not a concern
severity_signals.mild: occasionally feels they look tired or older
severity_signals.moderate: regularly bothered by looking older; compares to peers
severity_signals.severe: looking older is a persistent distress affecting confidence or work

drill_down: Which features signal age to them
Whether others comment on tiredness or age
Whether it affects work or relationships
What they hope treatment will change
